name: Permanent Residence & PR Card

requirements.blocker_text: PR is obtained via one of the economic (Express Entry, PNP), family, or humanitarian routes — there is no standalone 'PR application' independent of those categories.

This requires meeting the residency obligation of 730 days physical presence per rolling 5-year period to maintain PR status (exemptions apply for accompanying a Canadian-citizen spouse abroad, qualifying overseas employment with a Canadian business, and certain public-service work).

evidence_required.document: 730-day physical presence evidence per rolling 5-year period (for PR card renewal)

outcome.duration_length: indefinite status; PR card itself renewed periodically (typically 5 years)
outcome.physical_presence_requirement: 730 days physical presence per rolling 5-year period to maintain status

sources.title: Get a Permanent Resident Card - IRCC

notes: PR CARD RENEWAL FEE $50 CAD (Form IMM 5444); apply within 9 months of expiry (applying earlier gets the package returned). Processing has recovered from the 2022-2024 backlog: roughly 28 days to 3 months in 2026 — a genuine and confirmed improvement worth flagging distinctly from Portugal's/Spain's ongoing backlog situations elsewhere in this dataset. An expired PR card does NOT mean lost PR status — the two are separate; from outside Canada, a Permanent Resident Travel Document (PRTD) is needed instead of relying on the card itself. This route functions as Canada's PR-hub equivalent to uk_ilr/de_niederlassungserlaubnis in structure, but is genuinely UNUSUAL among this dataset's hub routes in that it's explicitly NOT a separate application — PR is granted directly by the underlying economic/family/humanitarian route itself, and this file exists primarily to document the ONGOING maintenance obligation (730-day rule) and card mechanics rather than a standalone grant pathway.
